text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Wednesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- President Guntis Ulmanis is continuing his visit France and said he believes that co-operation between the two countries will develop in more specific areas.
- Prime minister Andris Shkele made a speech at the EBRD annual conference in London. Later in the day he met a group of British industrialists and finance experts.
- Welfare Minister Vladimir Makarov met the chairman of the board in charge of establishing energy tariffs to discuss how to cut gas tariffs for people on low incomes.
-The cabinet approved the purchase of 1,000 EBRD shares worth 6.65 million lats, part of the bank's schedule to increase its capital stock.
- Andris Argalis and Juris Ritins have been elected vice-mayors of Riga.
- Latvia declined a request from the U.S. and Denmark to support a U.N. resolution condemning violation of human rights in China.
- The Danish government allocated 60 million crowns to support Poland and the Baltic States on their way to the EU.

- A Danish defence delegation arrived in Latvia. The head of the Latvian parliament European affairs committee, Edvins Inkens, said the visit signals to Russia that the Baltics have not been left in a so-called grey zone.
- Electricity company Latvenergo has tightened security after two bomb threats.
- Latvia's six major computer trading companies called on the cabinet to impose the VAT on computers being imported to Latvia.
- The EBRD's Transition Report Update ranks Latvia among those countries at a relatively advanced stage of transition.
- Riga city council decided to spend 2.8 million lats on building a new asphalt plant for the city.
